name: Workshop - Nimbus (Conversion Slide & Feature Velocity)
narrative:
Jordan Cole, a non-technical VP of Growth at a 15M-MAU mobile-first marketplace, opens the growth console and sees what the product squad has felt for three weeks: a cluster of user segments glowing red — conversion sliding after a checkout-flow change landed unevenly across platforms, every week of delay a lost slice of revenue. The event data is analytical, not served to the product, so the decision cycle is slow.

Jordan pulls up the worst segment: SEG-0000214, Gen-Z on Android, conversion down from 4.2% to 2.9% over three weeks — which feature should ship next to recover it? The assistant surfaces the driver (the checkout change hurt this segment specifically) and ranks the three plays (ship a variant that won a past experiment for a similar segment, ship an alternative variant, or roll out an existing feature flag that lifted a neighboring cohort), each with the projected conversion lift and the users at stake, from a heuristic scored on Nimbus's own experiment history. It recommends the proven variant, drafts the rollout note, and stops for approval. Jordan approves; the feature-flag decision writes back to Lakebase for the product to read at low latency, scale-to-zero for near-zero idle cost, with an audit trail and the assistant's AI spend capped against margin.

Workshop training template (Tech Summit FY27 Live Days): data generator + full spec set (SDP pipeline, metric views, conversion-lift model, dashboard + Genie, and a Databricks App with a Visualize/Assist/Act agent loop over Lakebase). Maps to the three build milestones — Lakebase, Databricks Apps, Unity AI Gateway.
